items.prompt: Premium escalations need a high completeness floor; routine requests use a short schema and strict budget. A small model passes routine but misses premium, while routine outputs are verbose. Which optimization is appropriate?
constraints: Quality floors are measured separately for premium and routine work.
Premium work cannot be silently downgraded.
Output tokens and spend can be validated by workload.

options.text: Route every request to the small model and accept the lower premium completeness.
Raise a global output limit for both workloads so premium and routine paths share one budget and schema.
Route premium to a model meeting its floor, tune routine output, and recheck slice quality and spend.
Use the cheapest model for all traffic and rely on user feedback to detect premium misses.

feedback.Reason: Optimization must preserve the premium floor while removing measured routine waste; a single global model or limit violates one workload’s contract.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends reducing spend while preserving quality and identifies token hygiene as a way to remove unnecessary usage.
Details.scenarioApplication: Select a model that clears premium completeness, constrain routine output against its schema, and compare cost and quality separately for each slice.
Details.errorCorrection: Downgrading premium and raising a global limit either breaches quality or spends more without addressing routine verbosity.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If both workloads passed the same floor on the small model and shared latency requirements, a common budget could be defensible.
Details.transfer: Optimize within workload-specific quality boundaries and verify cost changes against the quality slice that owns the risk.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: It knowingly violates the premium completeness floor.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A global limit preserves neither routine efficiency nor workload-specific quality evidence.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: User feedback is too late and does not make an untested quality downgrade safe.

items.prompt: Prompt-cache reads fall from 88% to below 10% after a unique request timestamp is inserted at the front of an otherwise stable system prompt. Document and policy content are unchanged, and cache-write tokens spike. What should the team change?
constraints: The stable prefix is otherwise byte-identical.
Repeated cases can verify cache-read fields.

options.text: Increase cache TTL while leaving the timestamp at the front of the prefix.
Move the timestamp to metadata or the newest turn and verify cache reads.
Switch to a larger model so it can reuse a changing prefix more effectively.
Remove the policy content from the prefix to make the cache key shorter.

feedback.Reason: A moving byte at the front changes the reusable prefix for every request; relocating request-specific metadata restores prefix stability.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says per-request text ahead of a stable prefix makes each request a full cache write and advises putting moving text in the newest user turn.
Details.scenarioApplication: Move the timestamp out of the stable prefix, repeat identical cases, and inspect cache-read and cache-write fields before further tuning.
Details.errorCorrection: TTL and model changes do not make unequal prefixes equal, and deleting policy content damages context rather than fixing the key boundary.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the prefix were unchanged and reads still fell, inspect TTL, breakpoint, model, or cache availability instead.
Details.transfer: Keep reusable context byte-stable and place request-specific values at the latest appropriate boundary.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: TTL cannot make each timestamped prefix identical to the prior prefix.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Model size does not change the cache key bytes.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Removing policy context trades correctness for a shorter but still unstable or incomplete prefix.

items.prompt: A publisher generates 40,000 summaries overnight while a separate editor chat must remain interactive; quality floors cannot be lowered. Select TWO cost and latency controls.
constraints: Batch latency is acceptable for overnight summaries.
Interactive latency matters for the editor chat.
Token and cache use can be measured on both paths.

options.text: Use batch processing for the overnight summaries and measure its quality and completion cost separately.
Use the least expensive model for every request without a quality comparison.
Raise the interactive output limit so it can absorb overnight work.
Disable caching on the editor path to simplify accounting.
Keep the editor path interactive and tune stable-prefix caching or token hygiene there without lowering its quality floor.

feedback.Reason: The two workloads have different completion contracts, so batch execution fits the overnight path while caching or token hygiene can reduce interactive spend without changing quality.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic identifies prompt caching and token hygiene as quality-preserving cost levers and notes that batch processing trades latency for its discount.
Details.scenarioApplication: Submit overnight work to batch and verify its quality, while measuring stable-prefix reuse and token budgets on the editor path.
Details.errorCorrection: An untested global model downgrade, larger limit, or disabled cache either risks quality, increases spend, or removes a useful lever.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every request required immediate streaming, batch would violate the contract and caching or token hygiene would be the available levers.
Details.transfer: Choose cost mechanisms per workload’s latency contract and preserve the quality boundary while measuring the result.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: A cheaper model can breach the quality floor when no comparison is supplied.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A larger interactive limit increases spend and does not process overnight work.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Disabling cache removes a quality-preserving cost lever without addressing workload timing.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Batch fits work that can wait and permits separate quality and cost accounting.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Interactive caching or token hygiene reduces repeated spend while preserving the user-facing latency contract.

items.prompt: An interactive compliance conversation needs fast first output, while a ten-minute reconciliation job can be polled later; both reuse policy and tool context. Which execution design fits these contracts?
constraints: The conversation and reconciliation job have different completion needs.
Stable repeated context can be measured in each request shape.

options.text: Use one synchronous request for both paths and raise max_tokens until reconciliation completes on the same connection.
Batch the interactive conversation so its lower price offsets the added wait.
Disable shared context reuse because the two consumers have different latency needs.
Stream interactive work, poll reconciliation asynchronously, and cache stable context per request shape.

feedback.Reason: Transport and execution mode should follow the consumer’s completion contract; each path can still reuse stable context in its own request shape.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends streaming for long-running interactive requests and Message Batches for work that can be polled instead of holding an uninterrupted connection.
Details.scenarioApplication: Stream the conversation, enqueue reconciliation for polling, and measure cache reuse independently for the two payload layouts.
Details.errorCorrection: One synchronous path risks timeout, batching the conversation adds unacceptable wait, and disabling reuse discards a measurable cost lever.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If reconciliation had to return before the user left the page, it would need an interactive streaming or shorter bounded workflow.
Details.transfer: Select transport and execution mode from the user’s usable completion boundary, then optimize shared context within each mode.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A single long synchronous request can time out and gives neither path its appropriate contract.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Batching the interactive path delays the first usable response.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Different latency contracts do not require abandoning stable context reuse.

items.prompt: A support agent’s cost per resolved case doubles while per-call input and output tokens stay stable. Traces show retries repeatedly run the same retrieval and validation tools. What should the team change first?
constraints: Tool calls and retry attempts can be counted per resolved case.
Successful and failed loops can be compared.
A maximum action or spend budget can be enforced.

options.text: Switch to a cheaper model for every call while preserving the unchanged retry loop and tool sequence.
Shorten the response limit so each repeated call costs fewer output tokens.
Deduplicate repeat tools, bound retries and steps, and recheck resolved-case cost and quality.
Retry more often so transient failures resolve before the case is abandoned.

feedback.Reason: The measured cost increase is repeated tool work per successful outcome, so deduplication and bounded recovery target the cause while preserving resolution quality.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic documents distinct errors, retry-after semantics, exponential backoff for transient failures, and a spend-cap condition; loop limits and deduplication are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Count repeated calls, reuse safe retrieval results, stop after the action or spend budget, and compare resolved-case cost and quality before and after.
Details.errorCorrection: Model price, response length, and more retries leave the amplification path intact or may worsen it.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If tool calls per resolved case were stable and cost rose with input tokens, context pruning or cache-prefix inspection would be the next hypothesis.
Details.transfer: Optimize cost per successful outcome and remove repeated work before changing model capability or user-visible quality.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Model price does not remove duplicate retrieval and validation calls.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Shorter prose leaves repeated tool executions and can reduce useful resolution evidence.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: More retries amplify the measured loop and spend.

items.prompt: A low-volume workflow has a short shared prefix and receives requests too far apart for repeated cache reads. Billing measurements show cache-write and cache-read charges plus setup latency are equal to or greater than uncached input cost, while quality is unchanged. Which initial cost decision fits the measured route?
constraints: Per-request input tokens, cache reads and writes, request spacing, setup latency, quality slices, and Usage API cost dimensions are available for a controlled before/after comparison.

options.text: Keep caching on every route because a stable prefix is generally cheaper, regardless of measured reuse and setup cost.
Make the prefix longer by adding optional policy text so each cache write contains more context.
Move every request to batch processing even though this route has an interactive latency requirement.
Disable caching on the low-volume route; keep the stable prompt for quality and monitor uncached cost and latency against the same quality floor.

feedback.Reason: Disable caching for this low-volume short-prefix route, retain the stable prompt shape if it helps quality, and monitor uncached cost and latency against the same quality floor before reconsidering. The decisive constraint is Prompt caching is a cost lever only when a stable prefix is reused often enough to amortize its writes and reads; measured low reuse and a short prefix reverse the default optimization choice.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic identifies prompt caching and token hygiene as quality-preserving cost levers and notes that batch processing trades latency for its discount. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Disable caching for this low-volume short-prefix route, retain the stable prompt shape if it helps quality, and monitor uncached cost and latency against the same quality floor before reconsidering.
Details.errorCorrection: The stated billing measurements show no amortization, and adding optional text increases cache writes and context cost without improving quality. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If traffic reused a long stable prefix frequently and cache-read savings exceeded writes and setup latency while quality stayed constant, caching would be the appropriate cost lever.
Details.transfer: Choose a cost lever from route-level reuse and outcome evidence, and keep quality and latency boundaries visible.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: The route’s measured writes, reads, and setup latency do not amortize caching, so a general rule is not evidence here.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Optional text increases cache and input work without fixing the measured lack of reuse.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Batch may reduce cost but changes the latency contract and is not the stated route decision.
